dm_a1:
We had no eval set at the time, so we used manual review to keep the clearly broken answers out.
- Three of us reviewed **200 answers** in two weeks, covering the six questions users asked most.
- The most common failure was **missing information**, not made-up facts, so we fixed the required fields in the prompt first.
- We skipped automated eval because there was no labeling budget. We traded people's time for speed and added it after launch.
dm_a2:
It wasn't a calculation. We stopped when new failure types stopped appearing.
- The first 80 answers surfaced five kinds of failure. The next 120 added only one more.
- So we stopped at 200 and spent the remaining time fixing rather than sampling.
dm_q1: Before launch, how did you make sure the model output was good enough to ship?
dm_q2: How did you decide 200 was enough?
dm_x1:
Two weeks for three people, roughly a quarter of that iteration's capacity.
- Worth it: the errors it caught were the kind that make people cancel.
- Once automated eval landed, manual review dropped to a weekly calibration pass.
